findings.description: The homepage hero badge reads "v0.2.0 · pre-1.0, API may move · core + 3 more on npm", and the Status section (lines 748 and 754) repeats the same stale claim in prose ("Four packages (core, testing, react, promise) are published at 0.2.0; the rest ship at 0.1.0, not yet on npm") and in a version chip ("0.1.0 – 0.2.0"). The actual state (package.json, verified in PRODUCT.md) is that all nine packages are published at 0.4.0 as of 2026-09-06. This is exactly the publish-status drift class scripts/check-publish-status.mjs (pnpm check gate 24) exists to catch, but that gate's TARGETS list only checks README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, spec/roadmap.md and apps/website/PRODUCT.md — it does not check apps/website/src/pages/index.astro, so this page's own marketing copy slipped through un-caught and now misleads a homepage visitor about the library's release maturity.
findings.suggestedFix: Update the hero badge and Status section copy to reflect 0.4.0 / all nine packages published, and add apps/website/src/pages/index.astro (or derive the badge text from landing-content.js at build time) to check-publish-status.mjs's TARGETS so this can't silently drift again.

findings.description: The Status section's stat row reads "merge gate: 22 checks", but the Proof section directly above it on the same page (bars.map, backed by the `merge gates passing` entry in src/data/landing-content.js line 140) displays "24 / 24", and PRODUCT.md's Evidence on Hand section states "24 total merge gates". spec/process/definitions-of-done.md's table currently lists 24 numbered steps. So the same page contradicts itself about how many gates exist.
findings.suggestedFix: Change "22 checks" to "24 checks" (or derive it from the same source as the Proof section's 24/24 bar so the two can't diverge again).

findings.description: The Compliance page's evidence table and its "What Qadi assembles" section (line 482, "chain-integrity checking across sequence numbers") both still use "chain-integrity" language for INV-QD-054. spec/invariants.md's changelog (entry 1.27) records that the underlying function/error were deliberately renamed from `verifyChainIntegrity`/`ChainIntegrityError` to `verifySequenceIntegrity`/`SequenceIntegrityError` specifically because "chain-integrity" reads as cryptographic tamper-evidence to a compliance reviewer and is not (see packages/audit/src/SequenceIntegrity.ts's own doc comment). The Compliance page is precisely the document aimed at that GxP/compliance-reviewer audience, so it is the one place on the site where this exact misleading term should least appear. The same stale term also appears in apps/website/src/content/docs/docs/packages/audit/capabilities.md line 3 (frontmatter description) and apps/website/src/content/docs/docs/packages/audit/index.md line 28, even though capabilities.md's own body text (lines 55-62) already correctly uses "Sequence integrity"/`verifySequenceIntegrity`.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace "chain-integrity" with "sequence integrity" in compliance.astro (lines 482, 614), capabilities.md's frontmatter description, and audit/index.md line 28, matching the renamed terminology already used in capabilities.md's body and in the actual source.

findings.description: The one code example on @qadi/react's overview page (using Can, QadiProvider, makeQadiAtoms) is fenced as ```jsx. scripts/lib/extract-code-fences.mjs (shared by check-doc-examples.mjs and check-website-doc-examples.mjs, gate 22) only extracts and compiles ```typescript and ```tsx fences — ```jsx is not in COMPILED_EXTENSIONS, so this snippet is silently skipped by the merge gate and never checked against the real API. Every other JSX example in this same docs tree (e.g. packages/react/hooks.md lines 42 and 111) correctly uses ```tsx and does get compiled (with `declare const` stubs for the pattern used throughout docs/concepts/*.md). This one page is the outlier, so a future prop rename on Can/QadiProvider/makeQadiAtoms would not be caught here the way it would be everywhere else.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert the fence to ```tsx and add `declare const`/import stubs for AppLayer, currentUser, canPublish, PublishButton and Disabled (matching the pattern already used in docs/concepts/*.md) so it compiles under check-website-doc-examples.mjs.

findings.description: starlight.css (Starlight's customCss, used by every /docs/* page) loads the same Google Fonts stylesheet via a plain CSS `@import`, which is render-blocking. src/components/HeadFonts.astro — used by the homepage, blog, and compliance pages — implements a deliberate non-blocking pattern for the identical font URL specifically to avoid this (preconnect + preload + `media="print"`/`onload` swap, with a documented rationale that a plain blocking `<link>` "still can't paint any text until the CSS declaring it has loaded"). Docs pages get none of that optimization and pay the render-blocking cost the rest of the site was deliberately engineered to avoid.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the `@import` in starlight.css with the same preconnect+preload+swap `<link>` pattern HeadFonts.astro uses (Starlight supports injecting extra `<head>` tags via its `head` config option), or extract HeadFonts.astro's links into a partial both the marketing pages and Starlight's head config can share.

findings.description: This internal working doc claims "`pnpm spec:website-examples` type-checks every fenced ```ts`/```typescript` block" (repeated in the verification checklist at line 102). scripts/lib/extract-code-fences.mjs, which that command runs, explicitly does the opposite: its own doc comment says it extracts ```typescript and ```tsx blocks "ignoring ```ts fragments (an explicit opt-out for illustrative snippets)", and COMPILED_EXTENSIONS only maps `typescript`/`tsx`. A future page author following this checklist could believe a ```ts fragment they wrote is being verified when it never compiles.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct both mentions to say only ```typescript`/```tsx` fences are compiled, and that ```ts` is the deliberate uncompiled-fragment convention (matching AGENTS.md §12's own description).

findings.description: The `chrome ? (...) : (...)` branches (lines 32-73 and 75-114) render byte-for-byte identical brand-link/nav-toggle/nav-links/GitHub-pill markup, differing only in whether it's wrapped in a `<header class="site-nav">`. This component's own header comment explains it was extracted specifically because four pages had "already drifted" from hand-copying this same markup independently — the two branches here reintroduce that exact risk inside the one component meant to prevent it: a future edit to a nav link, aria attribute, or icon made in one branch and missed in the other would silently diverge the docs-header nav from the marketing-page nav.
findings.suggestedFix: Factor the shared inner markup (brand link, toggle button, nav-links list, GitHub pill) into one block and wrap it conditionally in the `<header>`, e.g. via a small inner component or a single JSX expression reused by both branches, rather than duplicating it.

findings.description: States Starlight's docs chrome exists for "wayfinding through ~26 pages". The actual docs content tree (apps/website/src/content/docs/docs/**/*.md) currently has 39 pages (20 Concepts pages per CONCEPTS-PLAN.md's own inventory, plus 15 Packages pages, 3 Reference pages, and the Getting Started index) — roughly 50% more than stated. This is an internal design-system doc, not user-facing, so the impact is limited to a future contributor's mental model of the docs' scope.
findings.suggestedFix: Update "~26 pages" to the current page count, or phrase it without a specific number to avoid future drift as more Concepts/Packages pages are added.

findings.description: The blog collection's default `author` is "Mohammad Almechkor" (one word, lowercase 'm'), matching the one existing blog post's frontmatter (src/content/blog/introducing-qadi.md line 5). Everywhere else on the site the same person is credited as "Mohammad AL Mechkor" (package.json's `author` field, and the copyright line repeated in index.astro line 834, blog pages, and PRODUCT.md's Brand Commitments). Purely cosmetic — the blog currently always sets `author` explicitly rather than relying on the default — but the two spellings of one name sitting in the same small site is worth reconciling.
findings.suggestedFix: Pick one spelling ("Mohammad AL Mechkor" matches package.json and the footers) and use it consistently in content.config.ts's default and any future blog post frontmatter.
